## Purpose and evidence standard

This note covers the Department of Home Affairs migration products in the
current PLIDA metadata. The metadata supplier code is `HA`; this guide treats
the user's "DHA" shorthand as the same Home Affairs source group.

Schema and value-domain claims below are deliberately labelled by evidence
level:

| Evidence label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Official | Backed by an official public source linked in this guide. |
| Local generator | Observed in the current `fplida` generator, tests, PLIDA metadata, or foundation files. Useful for implementation, but not a real-world calibration target unless separately sourced. |
| Unresolved | No official source or local code evidence was found in this pass. Do not use as a calibration fact. |

## Source documents

| Source | Use in this guide |
|---|---|
| `inst/plida_metadata/datasets.csv`, `products.csv`, `variables.csv` | Current DIL dataset, product, table, and variable inventory. |
| `R/generate_amep.R`, `src/rust/src/amep.rs`, `tests/testthat/test-generate_batch5.R` | Current AMEP generated schema and tested value ranges. |
| `R/generate_visa.R`, `R/generate_sdb.R`, `R/generate_travellers.R`, `R/generate_migrant_demographics.R` and matching Rust modules | Current local output schemas for visa, settlement, travellers, and migrant demographics. |
| [Home Affairs settlement reports](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/settling-in-australia/settlement-reports) | Official context for settlement reporting products. |
| [Home Affairs settlement reporting caveats](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/settling-in-australia/settlement-reports/settlement-reporting-caveats) | Official reminder that settlement reporting has scope and interpretation caveats. |
| [Settlement Database data dictionary PDF](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/settlement-services-subsite/files/settlement-database-data-dictionary.pdf) | Official SDB field/code source to consult before promoting SDB code values. |
| [AMEP client profile paper](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/paper-a-profile-amep-clients.pdf) | Official AMEP context, including AMEP client data period and historic program structure. |

## Source-backed coverage decisions

| Product area | What the research source supports | What is still not found |
|---|---|---|
| SDB permanent migrants | Home Affairs settlement reporting pages and the SDB data dictionary are the official anchors for settlement-record scope and SDB field/code interpretation. | I did not find a public source in this pass that proves the generated SDB category distributions or maps every generated Home Affairs compact value to an official code label. |
| AMEP | The AMEP profile paper is useful program context, and local PLIDA metadata contains ASLPR and hours concepts. | I did not find a public AMEP variable-level codebook or score-distribution source for the generated ASLPR/hours fields. |
| Visa and traveller products | Local PLIDA metadata provides variable names and current generated schemas. | I did not find a public Home Affairs codebook for generated visa subclass/reporting-group values or the generated traveller `1`/`2`/`3` quarterly status encoding. |

## Product inventory

The current PLIDA metadata lists five Home Affairs datasets and thirteen
products.

| Dataset | Products in metadata | Current fplida coverage |
|---|---:|---|
| `AMEP` | 7 | Generator writes `amep-client-03-19` and copies it to `amep-english-03-19`; the other AMEP products are metadata-only in this pass. |
| `MT_DEMOGS` | 1 | Generator writes migrant demographics. |
| `SDB` | 1 | Generator writes permanent migrant settlement records. |
| `TRAVELLERS` | 3 | Generator writes ERP/PP-style quarterly status summaries. |
| `VISA` | 1 | Generator writes visa records. |

## Variable-level schema register

Every generated variable observed in this pass for this guide is listed in
[`schema-registers/schema-register-home-affairs.csv`](schema-registers/schema-register-home-affairs.csv).
The register records R type, sampled generated missingness, sampled generated
domains/distributions, and direct PLIDA metadata matches. Treat those sampled
domains/distributions as implementation evidence only, not as official source
data.

A rendered variable evidence appendix for this guide is available at [`variable-evidence-appendices/home-affairs-variable-evidence.qmd`](variable-evidence-appendices/home-affairs-variable-evidence.qmd). It contains one row per generated variable with observed generated values or distributions, local metadata/crosswalk status, and unresolved-source caveats.

A stricter source-audited variable-code evidence register is available at
[`home-affairs-variable-code-evidence.csv`](home-affairs-variable-code-evidence.csv),
with a rendered companion note at
[`home-affairs-variable-code-evidence.qmd`](home-affairs-variable-code-evidence.qmd).
Use that register to distinguish official SDB/AMEP concept support, local
PLIDA/generator evidence, and public-codebook-not-found rows.

| Dataset | Generated variable rows | Direct PLIDA metadata matches | No direct PLIDA name match |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `AMEP` | 12 | 2 | 10 |
| `MT_DEMOGS` | 11 | 11 | 0 |
| `SDB` | 16 | 16 | 0 |
| `TRAVELLERS` | 3 | 1 | 2 |
| `VISA` | 16 | 16 | 0 |

Rows without a direct PLIDA match need a generated-name to DIL-name crosswalk
before they are treated as source variables. `generated-variable-crosswalk.csv`
now maps the AMEP ASLPR fields, AMEP enrolment year, AMEP compact hours total,
and the compact Traveller ERP/PP status strings to same-dataset local metadata
concepts. Those mappings do not make the generated compact columns official
source variable names.

## Generated schema and value domains

### AMEP

The local AMEP generator writes only a compact client/English product. The
local tests establish the hour and ASLPR ranges; those ranges should not be
treated as real AMEP distributions without checking the AMEP source paper or
source microdata documentation.

| Variable | Type | Expected values or distribution | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SYNTHETIC_AEUID` | Character ID | Home Affairs agency person key; non-missing for generated rows. | Local generator |
| `YEAR_OF_BIRTH` | Integer | Source spine birth year for eligible overseas-born persons. | Local generator |
| `HOURS_TOTAL` | Numeric | Tested generated range 50 to 510 hours. | Local generator; compacted from same-dataset AMEP year/quarter hours metadata such as `AMEP_2003` and `AMEP_2019_Q2`; official distribution still required for calibration |
| `ASLPR_SPEAKING_INITIAL`, `ASLPR_LISTENING_INITIAL`, `ASLPR_READING_INITIAL`, `ASLPR_WRITING_INITIAL` | Integer | Tested generated scores 0 to 5. | Local generator; same-dataset AMEP metadata crosswalks to `INITIAL_ASLPR_SPEAK`, `INITIAL_ASLPR_LISTEN`, `INITIAL_ASLPR_READ`, and `INITIAL_ASLPR_WRITE` |
| `ASLPR_SPEAKING_LATEST`, `ASLPR_LISTENING_LATEST`, `ASLPR_READING_LATEST`, `ASLPR_WRITING_LATEST` | Integer | Tested generated scores 0 to 5; latest is intended to be no worse than initial in the synthetic process. | Local generator; same-dataset AMEP metadata crosswalks to `LATEST_ASLPR_SPEAK`, `LATEST_ASLPR_LISTEN`, `LATEST_ASLPR_READ`, and `LATEST_ASLPR_WRITE` |
| `ENROLMENT_YEAR` | Integer | Synthetic program enrolment year; generated from arrival and age logic. | Local generator; same-dataset AMEP metadata crosswalk to `ENROLLED_FY` |

AMEP gaps: the current implementation does not separately generate the
metadata-listed AMEP activity, address, award-code, award, or full English
module schemas. Local metadata contains initial/latest ASLPR variables, but I
did not locate a public score-label/distribution source in this pass.

| `YEAR_OF_BIRTH`, `MONTH_OF_BIRTH` | Integer | Birth year and month; month should be 1 to 12. | Local generator |
| `SEX` | Categorical | Local generated sex category from spine. | Local generator; official code mapping unresolved |
| `COUNTRY_OF_BIRTH`, `CITIZENSHIP` | Categorical/code | Country-code style variables generated from spine/migration logic. | Local generator; official SDB dictionary should be used before calibration |
| `ARRIVAL_DATE`, `DATE_OF_GRANT` | Date | Synthetic arrival and permanent visa grant dates. | Local generator |
| `VISA_SUB_CLASS` | Categorical/code | Visa subclass code. | Local generator; official subclass coding unresolved in this pass |
| `PRINCIPAL_FLAG` | Categorical | Principal/non-principal applicant flag. | Local generator |
| `MARITAL_STATUS` | Categorical | Marital status generated by migration module. | Local generator; official value labels unresolved |
| `ENG_FLUENCY_SPUK` | Categorical/code | Spoken English fluency field. | Local generator; official value labels unresolved |
| `OCCUPATION` | Categorical/code | Occupation code field. | Local generator; code standard unresolved |
| `YRS_EDUC_PRI_HIGH`, `YRS_EDUC_UNIV` | Numeric/integer | Years of primary/high and university education. | Local generator |
| `LAST_ON_DAY` | Date | Last observed/status date in local product. | Local generator |

### Travellers

The local traveller product is a status summary, not raw border movement
episodes.

| Variable | Type | Expected values or distribution | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SYNTHETIC_AEUID` | Character ID | Home Affairs agency person key. | Local generator |
| `ERP_STATUS_QUARTERLY` | Integer vector/string | Rust constants map quarterly status to 1 = resident present, 2 = resident absent, 3 = not resident. | Local generator; compacted from same-dataset `ERP_STATUS_YYYYQn` metadata columns |
| `PP_STATUS_QUARTERLY` | Integer vector/string | Same local status code domain as ERP status. | Local generator; simplified compact form of same-dataset `PP_STATUS_YYYYMn` and census-night PP metadata columns |

Traveller gap: local PLIDA metadata confirms wide ERP/PP status-column
concepts, but no official public codebook was located in this pass for the
generated `1`/`2`/`3` quarterly status encoding. Use the local constants only
for fplida implementation checks.

## Research uses and limits

These products are useful for testing migration linkages, migrant cohorts,
visa-to-settlement histories, and migrant-specific service use in later
fplida builds. They are not yet strong calibration products. In particular,
SDB, visa subclass/report group, IELTS, occupation, and traveller status codes
need source-backed code tables before they are used for research-facing
examples.

## Build implications

1. Keep Home Affairs products parquet-only unless a downstream package consumer
   requires CSV.
2. Add regression tests for all generated HA products, not only AMEP, before
   promotion.
3. Treat local category domains as implementation contracts, not official
   statistical domains, unless the relevant Home Affairs dictionary is linked
   directly in the variable table.
4. For future synthetic builds, add a separate evidence file mapping SDB and
   visa codes to the official Home Affairs data dictionary/code tables.

## Validation checks to add

| Check | Evidence basis |
|---|---|
| AMEP hours remain within tested range 50 to 510. | Local test. |
| ASLPR fields are integers 0 to 5 and latest scores do not decline unless a real source says decline is possible. | Local test plus program logic; local AMEP metadata confirms ASLPR field concepts but not generated distributions. |
| SDB date consistency: `DATE_OF_GRANT >= ARRIVAL_DATE` where the synthetic design intends grant after arrival. | Local generator. |
| Visa dates: grant date should not precede lodged date. | Local generator. |
| Traveller quarterly status values must remain within local constants 1, 2, 3. | Local Rust constants. |
